newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak C.Bank says forex inflow no threat to crown.
newsitem.headline: Slovak C.Bank says forex inflow no threat to crown.

text.p: The Slovak central bank on Wednesday said inflows of some $200-300 million in foreign capital over the past month, attracted by a high interest rate differential, did not threaten the crown.
"The interbank market calmed down at the end of January and over February because of slower credit expansion and inflow of foreign sources," NBS Governor Vladimir Masar told a news conference.

"However, this (inflow), estimated at between $200 million to $300 million, does not represent a greater danger for the (NBS) foreign exchange policy thanks to more active use of the crown's fluctuation band," Masar said.
The central bank has repeatedly said it would use the crown's fluctuation band of plus/minus 7.0 percent more actively than it did last year to introduce larger risk for speculative funds.

Slovak interbank money rates jumped to record levels of around 27 percent in the first weeks of January after the NBS moved to rein in a rapidly growing money supply and cool off a consumption-led boom.

The NBS set new rules at the beginning of the year for foreign exchange positions for monetary purposes -- and penalties for breaching the measures -- in an attempt to reduce the sector's loan expansion.

Rates have since retreated, helped by the inflow of foreign funds playing on the interest rate differntial. The Bratislava Interbank Offered Rates (BRIBOR) ranged between 17.3-21 percent on Wednesday.

In afternoon trading on Wednesday, the crown was at 0.28 below parity with its mark/dollar basket, after the NBS matched the market at 1030 GMT, fixing it at 33.324 dollar 19.472/mark, or 0.47 percent below parity, after -0.64 percent on Tuesday.
